correctness.rationale: Log amplitudes L_j(t)=E_j logR-2^j t meet adjacently at T_i=(n-i)logR, separated by logR. Around T_i, scaled v=2^{i-1}(t-T_i), ratio of neighboring terms is s=e^{-v}; all nonadjacent components and their first two derivatives are O_n(R^-1) compared to dominant pair uniformly on compact v. For adjacent rates λ and 2λ, β=B(v)=(1+s)(1+4s)/(1+2s)²=1+s/(1+2s)², whose unique nondegenerate maximum is 9/8 at s=1/2, v=log2. C² convergence plus negative curvature yields nearby unique strict peak with claimed timing and height O_n(R^-1). Fixed separated transition times yield separate peak windows; midpoint between adjacent transition times is dominated by a single term, hence β→1. Independent exact rational n=3 R=100 verified two disjoint strict three-time peak brackets. The asymptotic theorem uses fixed n and R→∞, not simulation or any uniform-in-n bound.
